Africa. The world's second-largest continent, home to fifty-four recognized nations and over one billion people of immense cultural, linguistic, and ethnic diversity. Cradled by human evolution and the birthplace of the world's oldest civilizations, Africa was subsequently subjected to European colonial partition, resource extraction, and the transatlantic slave trade—legacies that profoundly shaped its modern political and economic trajectories.

Africa is surrounded almost entirely by ocean: the Atlantic Ocean to the west, the Indian Ocean to the east, the Mediterranean Sea to the north, and the Red Sea to the northeast. Only the Suez Canal links it to Asia by narrow waterway. The Sahara Desert, stretching across North Africa from the Atlantic to the Red Sea, is the world's largest hot desert. Historically a major barrier to cross-continental contact, it has created distinct North African and sub-Saharan regions. The Nile River flows northward through northeastern Africa into Egypt and is the world's longest river. It has sustained Egyptian civilization for millennia. Other major rivers include the Congo River, Zambezi River, and Niger River. Africa straddles the equator and comprises diverse climatic zones: tropical rainforests in Central Africa, savanna grasslands in East and Southern Africa, Mediterranean climates in the north, and vast deserts. Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest peak.

The transatlantic slave trade, lasting from the fifteenth to nineteenth centuries, forcibly relocated approximately twelve million Africans to the Americas, devastating populations and societies. European powers partitioned Africa during the Age of Exploration and the Scramble for Africa, roughly from eighteen eighty to nineteen twenty, establishing colonies and exploiting mineral wealth and agricultural production. These powers drew arbitrary borders that persist today and underlie many modern conflicts. Africa is extraordinarily resource-rich, possessing vast reserves of petroleum, gold, diamonds, copper, and other minerals, along with enormous agricultural potential and freshwater reserves. Yet much of this wealth has been extracted by foreign corporations and powers. Modern Africa comprises vast cultural diversity: over two thousand languages are spoken, multiple religious traditions including Islam, Christianity, traditional religions, and Judaism coexist, and nations struggle with post-colonial state-building, economic development, and geopolitical positioning. The Atlantic Ocean borders Africa to the west and was the route for the transatlantic slave trade and European exploration.
